overview_markdown:
SmallClaw is a local-first AI agent framework built in TypeScript, positioned as an open-source alternative to cloud AI assistants. It supports multiple providers — Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, OpenAI API, and OpenAI Codex OAuth — allowing fully local or hybrid setups with no API costs and no data leaving the machine by default.

Its core architectural bet is a single-pass chat handler: one LLM call decides whether to respond conversationally or invoke tools, rather than running separate planning, execution, and verification agents. This reduces latency and works better with small models that struggle with multi-step orchestration. Tooling includes file operations with line-level edits, multi-provider web search (Tavily, Google, Brave, DuckDuckGo), Playwright-powered browser automation, terminal access, persistent session memory, and a drop-in SKILL.md skills system.

Compared to OpenClaw, SmallClaw trades ecosystem breadth and polish for simplicity and small-model efficiency. Recent commits show active development — v1.1 brought a system overhaul, and v1.0.4 added security hardening, Docker improvements, sub-agents, and a Telegram file browser — but the project lacks a clear license, official GitHub releases, and a significant community footprint.
